title: Home Entertainment
goal: Choose something to watch or play, discuss controls and device problems, and negotiate a break or stopping time.

here means the screen or application has stopped responding, not that it is cold.

runs.text: here means you beat or caught the speaker in the game.
can express annoyance or surprise; it is an impolite expression that some listeners find offensive. It can be an active choice among people comfortable using it.
expresses the same immediate reaction without that word. Neither phrase has to be directed angrily at the other player.
For another scene, a household has agreed to stop playing at eight. It is now eight, and one player asks for five more minutes.

runs.text: Okay, until eight oh five. Then we're stopping.

turns.en: Okay, until eight oh five. Then we're stopping.

turns.speaker: B
turns.en: Deal.

blocks.caption: Play, pause and negotiate · A & B

runs.text: No, we need to stop now
accepts the stated arrangement. Asking for more time does not itself extend the agreement.
Alone, play both speakers. Use the available titles, episode information and stopping-time facts; no video or recording is required.
You want something short, but your partner does not want sports. Suggest a choice, negotiate and agree on one available program.
Ask for episode 2. Give the unavailable reply and offer the movie or stopping. Decline the movie because of its length.
Ask for louder dialogue and subtitles. Reply and check whether the change helps.
Lose a race and react. Then ask for a break. Choose language that fits the imagined relationship.
Ask for five more minutes at eight. Rehearse both agreement until eight oh five and refusal. Respond to the actual answer.

“Let's try the first detective episode.” / “Episode two isn't available yet. Would you rather watch the movie or stop?” / “Could you turn the volume up a little?” / “Ah, you got me again! I'll be right back.” / “Okay, eight oh five, then we stop.” / “All right. I'll stop now.”
Return later with the models covered and reverse the preferences. Check whether you negotiated an activity and responded to your partner rather than reciting every option.
